Hi Tom — thanks for the details and the SOW. Below is a compact, line-item breakdown tailored to the pilot and to a potential 24-month commit. See attached spreadsheet (RDW-vpc-pricing-breakdown.xlsx) for the cell-level math.

Summary (pilot / initial quote):
- One-time On‑Prem License (per environment): $120,000 (per cluster) — CAPEX
- Platform Fee (annual): $48,000 / year — covers control plane, model catalog access, telemetry, and minor feature backports — OPEX
- Support (options):
  • Silver — Standard business hours (8x5) — $12,000 / year — response SLA P3/P4 only
  • Gold — 24x7 email + 9×5 phone for Sev2 — $36,000 / year — includes quarterly health checks and config reviews
  • Platinum — 24x7 phone + dedicated TAM, quarterly on‑site if requested — $120,000 / year

Discounting & credits we can offer (initial ask):
- 24‑month firm commit (platform fee): 10% off platform fee when prepaid annually (applies to OPEX line)
- Onboarding credit: we can offer a one‑month platform fee credit (capped to one environment) if Acme handles >80% of infra work and we provide remote enablement only
- Volume discount: for >3 clusters, additional 7% off one‑time license line

Notes re sizing: With sustained QPS of ~150 and 600 burst, recommended serving pool is 2 x 80GB A100-class instances (quantized weights) with autoscale to 4 during bursts. That configuration is reflected in the worksheet and is what the licensing / platform-fee assumptions are based on. If you expect persistent >300 QPS sustained, we should re-evaluate licensing tier.

Next steps: can you confirm (a) expected number of clusters for pilot, (b) whether Acme will prepay platform fees, and (c) who on your side will sign the SOW? I can loop Legal/Finance internally once we lock discount approach.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick 20-min commercial call if helpful.

Best,
Chloe Martin
Account Executive, Enterprise

Folks — forwarding Acme's ask plus my proposed commercial structure (see spreadsheet). Deal details: ACME-2026-1120.

Ask: Can we approve 12% off platform fee for 24-month prepaid + a one-month onboarding credit (platform fee credit) for them? They will self-manage infra and want the credit to offset some infra validation hours. They are committed to a pilot with 2 clusters (us-west).

Why 12% vs 10%: this is a strategic customer in healthcare; the customer will sign a 24-month firm commit and is likely to expand to multi-cluster within 12 months if pilot meets latency targets. I pushed for 12% to keep the year-one economics attractive. Also proposed a volume discount (7%) for additional clusters which is standard.

Constraints to consider:
- Onboarding credit should be capped to one environment and one month — no open-ended credits.
- Any discount should be conditioned on 2-year non-cancellable commit and prepayment schedule (or monthly + non-refundable deposit).

Please reply with approval or alternate guidance. If approved, I'll update the quote and loop Legal/Finance for DocuSign and SCC (SLA) addendum.

Forwarded message follows below for context.

Chloe — thanks for the write-up. Approve commercial direction with the following conditions: 

1) Approve 10% baseline discount on platform fee for 24-month prepaid. We can stretch to 12% if Sales agrees to a commercial clawback if they expand <1 cluster in year 2 (i.e., minimum committed clusters).
2) Onboarding credit approved: one-month platform-fee credit, capped to one environment. Must be explicit in SOW with no retroactive extensions.
3) Any Platinum-level SLA or on‑site obligations must be signed off by Legal (specifically for healthcare regulatory posture). Don't promise on-site TAM days until Legal signs the addendum.

I've attached the margin calc for reference — keep the list price for support and platform fee visible on the quote so Finance can track the discount.
